source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
This campus is the fourth-largest published data center by IT capacity in Texas, holding 36 MW of a state total of 475 MW across 19 disclosed facilities. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this capacity translates to roughly 900 racks, though the operator publishes no tenant mix or utilization. The technical footprint of 296,000 square feet suggests a mature multi-building campus designed for conventional enterprise and cloud workloads before the recent acceleration in AI compute demand.

The facility qualifies to host regulated workloads including healthcare data, government systems under FISMA, and payment card processing, which constrains but does not prevent AI deployment. These certifications indicate the campus was built for compliance-sensitive customers rather than purpose-built for accelerator-dense training clusters. No power infrastructure details are published, so the actual grid connection capacity, backup generation, and whether the 36 MW ceiling reflects campus power delivery or IT-only equipment limits remains unknown.

Texas ranks second nationally in published data center capacity, and this campus represents 7.6 percent of the state's disclosed MW. The state's 19 facilities with published specs sit among 133 mapped locations, meaning most Texas data centers do not disclose capacity, leaving AI scaling bottlenecks in the state largely invisible. This campus matters to AI only if its power and density assumptions match emerging workloads, which the published data does not establish.
